places.name: Brooklyn, New York
places.what: Born to Sarah and Harris Copland; the family lived above and beside its Washington Avenue department store. The coordinates mark Brooklyn; the house itself has not been independently geolocated.

sources.title: Copland House: timeline compiled by Michael Boriskin
Vivian Perlis: The Man Behind the Music

places.name: Manhattan, New York
places.what: Crossed from Brooklyn for lessons in harmony and counterpoint with Rubin Goldmark. The point marks New York in general and does not show where Goldmark taught.

sources.title: Vivian Perlis: Goldmark lessons across the Brooklyn Bridge

places.name: Fontainebleau
places.what: Attended the new American Conservatory and discovered Nadia Boulanger’s harmony class.

sources.title: Vivian Perlis: The Man Behind the Music

places.name: Paris
places.what: Studied composition with Nadia Boulanger; through her met Serge Koussevitzky, who commissioned the organ symphony.

sources.title: Vivian Perlis: Paris studies and Koussevitzky

places.name: New York City
places.what: Returned from France in 1924. Kept his New York apartment and loft studio until moving to Sneden’s Landing in 1947; travel and summer residencies interrupted this base.

sources.title: Vivian Perlis: return to New York in 1924

places.name: Saratoga Springs, New York
places.what: Visited the Yaddo artists’ colony and completed Piano Variations there. Coordinates mark Saratoga Springs.

sources.title: Copland House: timeline, first Yaddo visit
Stephen Hough: Piano Variations, Hyperion booklet note

places.name: Mexico City
places.what: First Mexican visit, arranged by Carlos Chávez; visited the dance hall that inspired El Salón México.

sources.title: Aaron Copland Fund: El Salón México

places.name: Mexico City
places.what: Carlos Chávez conducted the Orquesta Sinfónica de México in the première of Short Symphony.

sources.title: Aaron Copland Fund: Short Symphony première

places.name: Tanglewood, Massachusetts
places.what: Taught at the Berkshire Music Center in its summer seasons, from its first season in 1940. The post was seasonal.

places.name: Cincinnati, Ohio
places.what: Eugene Goossens conducted the Cincinnati Symphony Orchestra in the first performance of Fanfare for the Common Man.

sources.title: Aaron Copland Fund: Fanfare for the Common Man

places.name: Library of Congress, Washington, DC
places.what: Martha Graham danced the première of Appalachian Spring in the Coolidge Auditorium; Louis Horst conducted thirteen instrumentalists.

sources.title: Aaron Copland Fund: complete ballet catalogue
Commons institution record: Library of Congress coordinates

places.name: Ossining, New York
places.what: Bought his first house, Shady Lane Farm, and lived there for eight years. The point marks Ossining.

places.name: Cortlandt, New York
places.what: Bought Rock Hill, his home for the remaining thirty years of his life. Coordinates mark the town of Cortlandt, not the house.

sources.title: Copland House: timeline, Rock Hill purchase

places.name: North Tarrytown (now Sleepy Hollow), New York
places.what: Died at Phelps Memorial Hospital Center. The point marks the village, which was later renamed Sleepy Hollow.
